title: BetrValheim
menu.more.ask: Open the mod page in your browser?
admin.no: Locked settings can only be changed by an admin.
why.either: Takes effect once “{0}” or “{1}” is on.
why.own: Takes effect once “{0}” is set to “{1}”.
why.off: Only takes effect while “{0}” is off.
settings.tagged: Rows marked “Server” apply to everyone and only an admin changes them; all others are yours alone.
TimersEnabled.d: Show remaining times when looking at a station.
TimerQueueTime.d: Estimated time with enough fuel and the current wind.
MultiCraftEnabled.d: Choose how many times to craft a recipe.
CraftingSearch.d: A search field over the recipe list of every crafting station: typing shows only items whose name contains the text. Yours alone.
batch.title: Craft multiple times
saved: Changes are saved as you make them.
ModEnabled.d: Turn all BetrValheim features on or off.
ScanInterval.d: How often stations are refilled and loose items are collected.
BuildDrawers.d: Item drawers in the hammer menu. Off: no new ones; built ones keep their contents and work on.
BuildFeedingTrough.d: The feeding trough in the hammer menu. Off: no new ones; built ones keep their contents and work on.
BuildBeeBoxes.d: Bee boxes in the hammer menu. Off: no new ones; built ones keep their contents and work on.
UseContainers.d: Take from chests near the station, or near you when crafting.
UseForeignPrivateContainers.d: Also use ward protected chests and drawers owned by other players.
drawer.name: Drawer
drawer.store: Use an item on it to decide what it holds
drawer.rejected: Drawers take no weapons, armour or tools
UseGroundItems.d: Also use loose materials lying on the ground.
CraftRange.d: Measured from you. Applies to chests, drawers and the ground alike.
KeepInContainer.d: Stations leave this many in every chest, drawer and stack. Crafting and building still use everything. 0: stations use all.
ReservedItems.d: Prefab names, separated by commas, the amount above is kept of. Empty keeps it of every item.
CraftFromContainers.d: Use nearby stored materials for crafting and upgrading.
BuildFromContainers.d: Use nearby stored materials with the hammer, hoe and cultivator.
AutoRepairEnabled.d: Repair everything worn as soon as you use a workbench.
ManualRefill.d: Use stations normally to add one material or fuel from nearby sources when you carry none. Uses Station supply range, source permissions, blocked items and reserves. Independent of automatic refill and crafting/building from containers.
RefillEnabled.d: Automatically top up stations from their own surroundings.
RefillFuel.d: Add coal, wood and other fuel.
StationChoice.d: Shift + E on a station that takes several materials (smelter, blast furnace) opens a window to tick which materials it is refilled with. Off: Shift + E is as in the game and every material is refilled. Only while Refill, Refill material and the station kind are on.
choice.note: BetrValheim refills only what is on. Shown is what lies nearby, and what is off. By hand you can put in anything.
choice.empty: None of this station's materials lies in its reach right now (F11 → Stations). Shown is what lies nearby, and what you switched off.
choice.off: Refilling material is off (F11 → Stations → Refill material); the choice counts once it is on.
RefillMaterial.d: Add ore, dough, food and other input.
StationSupplyRange.d: How far a station reaches into chests and drawers around itself.
BlockedStationItems.d: Never fetch these from sources for manual or automatic station filling. Internal names, separated by commas.
LazyCooking.d: Food that is done drops out of cooking stations and ovens by itself, before it can burn - as if taken with E. Only where food can burn in the game.
general.hint: The master switch, how often everything else runs, and your language.
sources.hint: Where items may come from — for crafting and for stations alike.
crafting.hint: What you build and craft yourself. The range is measured from you.
inventory.hint: Up to three more pages under your own inventory, and a page for your equipment. What lies there is kept when switched off.
ExtraInventory.d: Pages of eight by five, opening with your inventory. The mouse wheel turns them. Only one can be enabled at a time: Extra inventory or Backpack. Turn Backpack off before enabling Extra inventory.
MainInventoryFirst.d: What you pick up or take fills your inventory first, the pages once it is full. Only for you.
ExtraPageCount.d: 1 to 3. Fewer moves what lies on the pages taken away onto the others, then into your inventory.
ExtraInventoryWeight.d: How heavy the pages and the equipment page are, compared to the game. 0 weighs nothing, 50 half, 100 as in the backpack.
StackFactor.d: Every stackable item stacks this many times higher than in the game, 1 to 100 (2 makes 50 wood 100). Unstackable items stay single. Lowered again, stacks over the size are spread onto free slots when loaded; without a free slot they stay on their stack. Nothing is lost.
ItemWeight.d: What every item weighs, in percent of the game, in steps of 5: 100 as in the game, 50 half, 0 nothing. How much you can carry stays the same.
QuickStackEnabled.d: Stores what you carry in nearby chests and drawers that already hold it. Favourites: Alt-click.
RestockEnabled.d: Tops up ammunition, food and potions from nearby chests and drawers.
QuickStackRange.d: How far around you chests and drawers are used for storing and restocking.
QuickStackKey.d: Click, then press the key - alone or with Ctrl, Shift or Alt. Escape cancels.
RestockKey.d: Click, then press the key - alone or with Ctrl, Shift or Alt. Escape cancels.
FetchMaterialsKey.d: With the hammer, cultivator or hoe: the materials for one of the chosen piece come from chests, drawers and the ground in reach into your inventory. Click, then press the key - the middle and side mouse buttons work too.
MarkerShare: Share markers at the cartography table
MarkerShare.d: Writing to a cartography table shares your markers of the groups shown, as the game shares its own pins: whoever reads it sees them as map pins. Hidden groups stay yours.
MarkerSound.d: Setting a marker plays the writing sound of the cartography table, only for you.
qs.none: Nothing nearby holds what you carry.
switchoff.moved: Switched off - moved into your inventory:
switchoff.left: No room - kept until switched on again:
extra.title: Extra inventory
tidy.tight: Already packed as tight as it goes.
QuickSlotKey1.d: Key for quick slot 1 of the equipment page, alone or with Ctrl, Shift or Alt. A key the game already uses then does only this.
QuickSlotKey2.d: Key for quick slot 2 of the equipment page, alone or with Ctrl, Shift or Alt. A key the game already uses then does only this.
QuickSlotKey3.d: Key for quick slot 3 of the equipment page, alone or with Ctrl, Shift or Alt. A key the game already uses then does only this.
QuickSlotKey4.d: Key for quick slot 4 of the equipment page, alone or with Ctrl, Shift or Alt. A key the game already uses then does only this.
QuickSlotKey5.d: Key for quick slot 5 of the equipment page, alone or with Ctrl, Shift or Alt. A key the game already uses then does only this.
QuickSlotKey6.d: Key for quick slot 6 of the equipment page, alone or with Ctrl, Shift or Alt. A key the game already uses then does only this.
FoodSlotKey1.d: Key for food slot 1 of the equipment page, alone or with Ctrl, Shift or Alt. With the slot empty, the key does what it does in the game.
FoodSlotKey2.d: Key for food slot 2 of the equipment page, alone or with Ctrl, Shift or Alt. With the slot empty, the key does what it does in the game.
FoodSlotKey3.d: Key for food slot 3 of the equipment page, alone or with Ctrl, Shift or Alt. With the slot empty, the key does what it does in the game.
AmmoSlotKey1.d: Key for ammo slot 1 of the equipment page, alone or with Ctrl, Shift or Alt - Z, X, C or F1, say. A key the game already uses (X sit, C walk) then does only this.
AmmoSlotKey2.d: Key for ammo slot 2 of the equipment page, alone or with Ctrl, Shift or Alt - Z, X, C or F1, say. A key the game already uses (X sit, C walk) then does only this.
AmmoSlotKey3.d: Key for ammo slot 3 of the equipment page, alone or with Ctrl, Shift or Alt - Z, X, C or F1, say. A key the game already uses (X sit, C walk) then does only this.
EquipmentPage.d: Named slots for armour, cape, trinket, utilities, food, ammunition, keys and quick slots. Each takes only its own kind of item. Separate from Extra inventory; must be on to equip a backpack.
equipment.title: Equipment
slot.hint: Takes only this kind of item.
extra.unreadable: Your extra inventory could not be loaded. Nothing is lost - is a mod missing?
CollectEnabled.d: Collects loose items, including items you dropped, into assigned drawers or matching chests. Unassigned drawers are the optional fallback. A cart nobody is pulling collects as well.
CollectRange.d: How far a chest or drawer reaches for loose items around itself.
DrawersFirst.d: Where loose items are stored first, and where crafting, building and stations take from first. Your own inventory always pays first.
DrawerAutoAssign.d: An unassigned drawer claims items only when no assigned drawer or matching chest in collection range has room for the whole stack.
portals.hint: Walk into a portal and pick any other portal as the destination.
PortalPicker.d: On: walking into a portal opens the map and you pick any destination. Off: portals work like in the normal game, linked by name.
TravelRune.d: A rune from the artisan table that opens the portal picker from anywhere; read, it takes you to the chosen portal and is used up. Only with the portal picker on.
TravelRuneCost.d: What a travel rune costs: item names as the game knows them, each with its amount, separated by commas - SurtlingCore:1, Silver:1.
why.norunecost: No cost set: the travel rune cannot be made.
PortalsOnMap.d: Every portal is shown on the large map for every player. Off keeps other players' bases hidden.
PortalsOnMinimap.d: Every portal is also shown on the small map in the corner.
PortalNames.d: Names beside the portal markers on the map. The portal picker always shows them.
TamesThroughPortals.d: Tamed animals following you go through portals with you and keep following.
ProtectPortals.d: Portals take no damage – from monsters, weapons, fire or missing support – and monsters do not go for them. Only the hammer takes them down.
portal.title: Portal Network
portal.error: Could not load the portal list.
portal.hint: Click a destination in the list or on the map
stations.hint: What stations fetch for themselves, which stations may, and the time they still need.
storage.hint: Storage that collects by itself, quick stack and restock by key, and which of the mod's pieces may be built.
map.hint: Markers on the map and the compass at the top of the screen. Yours alone.
display.hint: How the world and your character look on your screen. Mist and sails are set by the server for everybody; the rest is yours alone.
keys.hint: Every key of the mod: click it and press the new one, alone or with Ctrl, Shift or Alt. Escape cancels. Yours alone.
Language.d: Language of this window. Auto follows the game language.
TrashBin.d: Show a bin in the corner of the inventory. What you drop on it is gone for good.
trash.label: Trash
MinimapLogo.d: Shows the BetrValheim logo just below the minimap. Only on your screen.
MinimapClock.d: Day and time of day in the game, in the lower right corner of the minimap, in 24 hours. Only on your screen.
EquipmentCharacter.d: Your character in the middle of the equipment page, wearing what you wear, turned with the mouse. Off: the figure.
AutoEquipArmor.d: Equip picked-up helmets, chest armour, leg armour and capes in empty slots, using the game’s equip time. Keeps worn or queued equipment. Only world pickups; excludes utility items and backpacks.
TooltipCompare.d: An item's tooltip shows how it differs from what you wear or hold in its place: armour, damage, block, durability, weight - green where better, red where worse.
SkillProgress.d: While a skill rises, a short line in the upper left with its level and how far it is to the next.
BetrSkills.d: Stronger skills: every skill learns 1.5 times as fast, and some raise a maximum with each level - Blocking health, Run and Dodge stamina, Elemental and Blood magic eitr, Woodcutting and Pickaxes carry weight. The same skills also refill their value faster, up to five times at level 100. Turning this feature off keeps your levels and removes its bonuses. Without the mod, the game's own skill levels remain. Combat tempo learns from damaging hits on living creatures and increases attack animation speed.
ArmorSetBonus.d: Every piece of the game's armour sets - helmet, chest and legs - adds max. health and stamina while worn, the mage sets eitr too: more for later biomes, heavy sets more health, light sets more stamina; one more per quality level. Armour values stay as in the game; capes and clothing add nothing.
DeathRespawn.d: With a Fuling totem in its slot on the equipment page (top left in the picture), dying asks where to rise: at your grave for one totem, or at your bed as in the game. That totem stays with you when you die.
rise.title: Rise at your grave?
rise.note:
Uses the Fuling totem in its slot.
Otherwise as usual: at your bed, without one at the start.
compare.title: Instead of {0}:
ShowHelmet.d: Off: your helmet is not shown, for you and for everyone else, and your hair and beard show. Only the look: worn, the helmet still counts with everything it gives.
SailOpacity.d: How solid sails are drawn, so you can see where you are going. 100 is the game's own sail, 0 none at all. Every ship; set by the server, the same for every player.
MistOpacity.d: How dense the mist is drawn. 100 is the game's own mist, 0 none at all. Set by the server, the same for every player.
LoadingScreen.d: BetrValheim's loading screen while the world loads. Off: the game's own.
ShowStatusMessages.d: Show a short message on screen after each refill.
VerboseLog.d: Write detailed diagnostics to the BepInEx log.
ToggleKey.d: Open or close this window. Click, then press the key.
qc.label: Quick Connect:
piece.ew_drawer_desc: Holds up to 10000 of a single kind of item by default (as the server sets it) and shows what it holds on its front.
piece.bv_beebox_desc: Built empty. Put a queen bee in with Shift+E. Up to four boxes side by side and stacked form one hive.
bee.noqueen: No queen yet - put one in through "Look inside".
bee.cold: The bees are too cold - a fire nearby warms them.
bee.newqueen: A new queen came out with the honey!
bee.queensonly: Only queen bees go in here.
bee.full: Every slot already has its queen.
TimerBeehives: Beehives, bee boxes and birds' nests
TimerBeehives.d: When the next product is ready (honey, feathers).
PortalsAllowAllItems: Allow ore and metal through portals
PortalsAllowAllItems.d: Like the world modifier: everything may go through portals. Off: the game's rule.
RepairAnywhere.d: Every crafting station repairs everything, at any level. Off: as in the game.
Salvage.d: Another tab at every crafting station: items made there are taken apart there and give back part of their materials, every quality level included. Not listed: what you wear, the hotbar (1-8) and items enchanted with Epic Loot by RandyKnapp and the Epic Loot Team. Batches such as arrows only whole.
SalvageReturn.d: Share of the materials taking an item apart gives back, rounded up. Worn items give as much as new ones.
salvage.empty:
Items made at this station that you carry can be taken apart here.

Not listed: what you wear and the hotbar (1-8).
salvage.enchanted: Enchanted: the enchantment is lost when taken apart.
DrawerTakeOneKey.d: Held with Use on a drawer: take one item, or release an empty drawer.
DrawerStoreAllKey.d: Held with Use on a drawer: store everything of its kind you carry.
MarkersEnabled.d: The marker key, the markers on the map and their list beside the large map.
MarkerKey.d: Sets a marker where you stand, named after what you look at. Click, then press the key.
marker.name: Name ...
marker.groups: Existing groups - a click takes one:
marker.exists: There is a marker of this name here already
marker.full: No more markers: {0} is the limit
markers.title: Markers
markers.sort.name: Sort: name
hud.hint: Everything this mod shows on the HUD. Positions in pixels of your game resolution, counted from the lower left corner. Yours alone.
HudSlotsMoved.d: Only with the BetrValheim HUD off: ammunition, food and quick slots beside the health bar. Auto: beside the health bar, as always. Own: at X and Y. With the BetrValheim HUD on, the slots stand in its diamonds and these settings are locked.
HudSlotsX.d: Only with the BetrValheim HUD off. Pixels from the left edge of the screen, at your game resolution. 0 = far left, end of the slider = flush right. Stays in the same place at another resolution. Type exact values into the field.
HudSlotsY.d: Only with the BetrValheim HUD off. Pixels from the bottom edge of the screen, at your game resolution. 0 = at the bottom, end of the slider = flush top. Stays in the same place at another resolution. Type exact values into the field.
Compass.d: A compass line at the top of the screen: the eight directions and a tick every 15° pass along it as you turn.
CompassMarkers.d: Your own markers as small diamonds on the line, in their direction: the 12 nearest within 500 m. The one nearest the middle shows its name and distance below.
CompassGrave.d: Your grave on the line, with its distance when you look towards it – from the death marker of your latest death. Once the grave is emptied and you stand there, the marker leaves the map too.
CompassBosses.d: The bosses you have found - shown on the map by a runestone - on the line in their direction, at any distance; the one you look towards with name and distance. Crossed out on the map: not shown.
CompassMoved.d: Auto: at the top middle. Own: at X and Y.
CompassX.d: Pixels from the left edge of the screen, at your game resolution. 0 = far left, end of the slider = flush right. Stays in the same place at another resolution. Type exact values into the field.
CompassY.d: Pixels from the bottom edge of the screen, at your game resolution. 0 = at the bottom, end of the slider = flush top. Stays in the same place at another resolution. Type exact values into the field.
FoldButton.d: The button at the top of the page rail that folds the extra pages and the equipment page away. Off: no button, the pages stay open.
PagesMoved.d: The extra pages and the equipment page with their rail; an open chest stands in their place. Auto: under the inventory, as always. Own: at X and Y.
PagesX.d: Pixels from the left edge of the screen, at your game resolution. 0 = far left, end of the slider = flush right. Stays in the same place at another resolution. Type exact values into the field.
PagesY.d: Pixels from the bottom edge of the screen, at your game resolution. 0 = at the bottom, end of the slider = flush top. Stays in the same place at another resolution. Type exact values into the field.
CornerHud.d: Health, eitr and stamina as three bars, the forsaken power, food and the BetrValheim Slots in diamonds - in place of the game's health panel.
CornerHudSize.d: 100: a food icon in it is as large as the game's own.
CornerHudMoved.d: Auto: where the game's health panel is. Own: at X and Y.
CornerHudX.d: Pixels from the left edge of the screen, at your game resolution. 0 = far left, end of the slider = flush right. Stays in the same place at another resolution. Type exact values into the field.
CornerHudY.d: Pixels from the bottom edge of the screen, at your game resolution. 0 = at the bottom, end of the slider = flush top. Stays in the same place at another resolution. Type exact values into the field.
StatusEffectList.d: The game's status effects, top right, as a list going down: icon, name and the time left in one row each. Off: the game's own tiles.
StatusEffectBars.d: In the list, under each effect that runs out, a bar with the time left. Effects without a duration get none.
piece.bv_trough_desc: Three slots for anything animals eat. Tame animals nearby eat from it when they are hungry; wild ones that can be tamed eat from it as from the ground, so it tames them too.
Backpack.d: A backpack made at the workbench, put on with a right click like a cape, into its own slot on the equipment page under the totem. Worn, it hangs on your back and has its own tab beside the pages. Off: none can be made, a worn one goes into your inventory and keeps what it holds. Requires Extra inventory OFF and Equipment page ON (F11 → Inventory), and Backpack ON (F11 → Backpack). Only one can be enabled at a time: Extra inventory or Backpack.
backpack.title: Backpack  (level {0})
backpack.unreadable: Your backpack's contents could not be loaded. Nothing is lost - is a mod missing?
piece.bv_backpack_desc: Put on with a right click, into its slot on the equipment page. Its tab grows with each level; picked up items go in first. What it holds stays in it, wherever it goes.
piece.bv_travelrune_desc: Read it, and the map opens with every portal: pick one and travel there from wherever you stand. Used up by the journey; ore and metal stay behind, as at a portal.
travelrune.off: Travel runes only work with them and the portal picker on (F11 → Portals).
travelrune.gone: The travel rune is no longer in your inventory.
backpack.hint: A backpack from the workbench, worn in its slot on the equipment page. How large each level is and what it costs is set here.
BackpackContentWeight.d: What lies in a backpack weighs, in percent of the game's weight. 100 is as heavy as in the inventory, 0 nothing.
BackpackPickupFirst: Picked up items into the backpack first
BackpackPickupFirst.d: What you pick up or take out of a drawer goes into the worn backpack first, then where it went before. Off: only what you put in by hand.
BackpackForCrafting.d: What lies in the worn backpack counts and pays for crafting and building, as the inventory does.
BackpackInBackpack.d: A backpack can be put into another one, with everything in it. Never into itself.
BackpackColumns.d: How many slots wide the backpack is at this level, 1 to 8.
BackpackRows.d: How many rows it has at this level, 1 to 5.
BackpackCostMake.d: What making it costs at the workbench: item names as the game knows them, each with its amount - LeatherScraps:2, DeerHide:2.
BackpackCost.d: What upgrading to this level costs, at a workbench of this level: item names as the game knows them, each with its amount - LeatherScraps:3, DeerHide:3.
BackpackOnBack.d: Worn backpacks hang on the players' backs - yours and everyone else's with BetrValheim. Off: you see none; only for you.
backpack.cantwear: Requires Extra inventory OFF and Equipment page ON (F11 → Inventory), and Backpack ON (F11 → Backpack).
backpack.inside: Take it out of the backpack first.
backpack.notinside: A backpack does not go into a backpack (F11 → Backpack → Backpack in a backpack).
backpack.noroom: No room to take the backpack off.
DrawerCapacity.d: How many items one drawer holds, 5000 to 100000. Lowered, a drawer holding more keeps it and only takes no more.
ChestCategories.d: Shift + E on a chest: give the chest categories, single items in or out, a priority and a name. Quick stack, tidying up and the chest's place stacks then put items into the chests made for them, even empty ones; with it, quick stack also puts spare weapons, tools and armour into chests made for them. Off: chests take what they already hold, as before; names are not shown.
ChestSortButton.d: Show an A-Z button on open chests. Sorts by the item names in your game language; keeps all stacks and their contents intact. Local, default off.
chestrules.name: Name
chestrules.items: Single items - a click switches: in, out, neither
chestrules.none: No categories: this chest takes what it already holds, as before.
chestrules.note: Takes what is green; priority {0}: lower numbers fill first.
chestrules.legend: Green: on · Yellow: part of it · Grey: off
why.nocost: No cost set: this level can be neither made nor upgraded to, and none above it.
letsbuild.hint: LetsBuild's settings. What the server sets only admins change; everything else each player sets for themselves.
betrtame.hint: BetrTame's settings. What the server sets only admins change; everything else each player sets for themselves.
world.hint: Rules of the world for everybody: what floats, when loot drops, what comes back. Only admins change them.
FloatingItems.d: Every item that falls into water or tar floats instead of sinking. Items already on the bottom come up when the area loads again.
FloatingExceptions.d: Items that keep sinking: their names as the game knows them, separated by commas - Stone, Flint.
InstantLoot.d: A creature's loot drops the moment it dies, not when its body vanishes. The body still falls and vanishes as before.
RegrowChests.d: Chests the world placed (dungeons, villages, camps) fill again from their own loot table some days after they were emptied, once their area loads again. Never chests players built.
RegrowCamps.d: Creatures the world places only once (camps, villages, dungeons) return some days after they died, once their area loads again. Not bosses, and not creatures carrying something for a quest or that may not go through portals.
RegrowDays.d: In-game days (20 minutes each) after which emptied chests and dead camp creatures return.
EnemyHealthNumber.d: The health bar over a creature shows its health as a number: now / most.
EnemyStars.d: Creatures with more than two stars show all of them: up to five as stars, beyond that one star and the number.
EnemyBarSize.d: Size of the health bar over a creature in percent, with its name, number and stars. 100: the game's. Not the boss bar at the top.
EnemyBarDistance.d: Up to how many metres the bar over a creature is shown. 30: the game's. As in the game, a creature shows its bar once you have looked at it (up to 50 m away), then for a minute. Bosses keep the game's 100 m.
betrskills.tempo.name: Combat tempo
betrskills.tempo.description: Train by hitting living creatures with melee, ranged or magic attacks. Each level adds 0.5% attack animation speed, up to +50% at level 100. Bow draw and crossbow reload times are unchanged.
CombatTempo.d: Train through damaging hits on living creatures: +0.5% attack animation speed per level, up to +50% at level 100; 0.25 XP per successful attack before learning bonuses, regardless of how many targets it hits. Needs BetrValheim skills. Off keeps your level and removes the speed bonus. Bow draw and crossbow reload times are unchanged.
